subject: Post-demo: model fit evals & parity thresholds
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model fit evals & parity thresholds

Thanks again for taking the demo today, Alicia — really appreciate the time. Short recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Recap: we covered Redwood Dedicated options, the quick model-swap demo, and the proposed eval workflow. You confirmed that PayGrid's key acceptance criteria are: parity vs your internal baseline on task accuracy, no significant regressions on entity extraction, and predictable latency for production traffic.

- Proposed eval scope (what we'll run):
  1) Run a 1k-sample model-fit eval on your canonical prompt set (attached: prompt_set_v2.jsonl).
  2) Compare two recommended open-model candidates (LlamaX-13B-int8, RedI-7B-4bit) against your proprietary baseline (PayGrid Base-1).
  3) Metrics: weighted accuracy (primary), QA F1 / exact match, hallucination rate, and latency P50/P95.
  4) Acceptance thresholds: can you confirm whether you want absolute parity (within 3% accuracy) or a looser threshold? We suggested <=3% delta as a starting point.

- Timeline: we can run an initial pass within ~10 business days after you share the labeled sample/labels and any specific scoring rules. We'll publish a dashboard link and the CSV of per-example outputs.

- Next steps we need from PayGrid:
  • Provide the labeled sample or a link to the S3 bucket (1k rows).
  • Confirm any hard rejection categories (e.g., PII leakage, specific hallucination types).
  • Confirm latency SLOs (e.g., P95 < 500ms).

Attaching prompt_set_v2.jsonl (sample prompts + category tags). I'll loop in Marissa and Aditya to own the eval execution and results. Happy to jump on a quick sync next week to review results.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
--
Attachment: prompt_set_v2.jsonl (JSONL, 1k rows sample)

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: PayGrid ML Team <ml@paygrid.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit evals & parity thresholds

Thanks Lauren — great demo, and the proposed plan sounds right. A few clarifications and notes from our side: 

- Acceptance thresholds: our bar is fairly high on accuracy for the payments reconciliation flow. We want weighted accuracy within 2-3% of our baseline on the primary task. For entity extraction (merchant names, amounts), we absolutely need no more than a 1% drop in F1. If the open model exceeds hallucination or entity drop beyond that, it will be a blocker.

- Latency: for real-time suggestions we target P95 < 400ms but we'd accept up to 500ms for an initial rollout.

- We've uploaded a small labeled sample with expected outputs here: s3://paygrid-evals/sample_labels.csv (attached sample: paygrid_sample_labels.csv). It includes tags for tricky edge cases and our scoring rubric.

- Security: please confirm that Redwood will not persist the raw PII fields in logs for this eval. We can provide a sanitized subset if needed.

Happy to have the PayGrid ML team onboard the results review — let's tentatively plan for a review call the week of Jun 14.

— Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Data Science | PayGrid
agomez@paygrid.com
--
Attachment: paygrid_sample_labels.csv (CSV, 250 rows sample)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Alicia Gomez <agomez@paygrid.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit evals & parity thresholds

Looping in recommended eval plan and model candidates. Per the ask, here's a concrete plan we can execute: 

1) Model candidates (initial run):
   - LlamaX-13B-int8 (open candidate; good tradeoff for structured QA + entity extraction)
   - RedI-7B-4bit (smaller, for latency-focused baseline)
   - PayGrid Base-1 (your baseline; we'll run against the provided labeled set)

2) Eval metrics and acceptance rules:
   - Primary: weighted task accuracy (aggregate by category) — target: within 3% absolute of PayGrid baseline.
   - Secondary: entity extraction F1 (merchant, amount) — target: no more than 1% absolute drop.
   - Hallucination rate: measured as percentage of confident-but-incorrect assertions — must not exceed 2x baseline.
   - Latency: P50/P95 measured on Redwood Dedicated infra; suggested P95 <= 500ms for initial pass, target <400ms for production.

3) Data handling and privacy:
   - We'll only store hashed IDs and anonymized labels during the eval run; raw PII fields will be excluded from persistent logs unless you provide sanitized data.

4) Deliverables and timeline:
   - Deliverable: per-example CSV, aggregate dashboard, and recommended configuration (model + quantization + batching).
   - Timeline: 7-10 business days once we have the 1k labeled sample and scoring rubric.

Attachments: open-models-benchmarks.pdf (summary of recent bench runs), redwood_eval_plan.md (detailed steps and scripts).

I'll kick off the evaluation as soon as we get the S3 link with the labels and confirmation on acceptance thresholds. If PayGrid needs a stricter threshold, call that out and we'll prioritize quality over latency.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
--
Attachments: open-models-benchmarks.pdf; redwood_eval_plan.md
